evals.prompt: Plan a Meta lead campaign for a payroll-compliance consultation. We have a GBP 600 cap, an approved Brand Kit, a ready landing page, and want to compare three copy angles for UK founders. Keep the first test small and do not launch anything.
evals.expected_output: Creates one approval-ready campaign ticket with a falsifiable thesis, small controlled variation plan, conditional copy route, distinct approval gates, measurement and read-only check-in handoff; does not launch, spend, or create a duplicate program.
assertions: Creates a canonical ticket rather than a second plan schema
Uses Ad Advisor for strategy and Social Content for copy
Does not require a Tasty Pack or Asset Advisor for a copy-only test
Separates plan and launch approvals

evals.prompt: Turn our B2B security offer into a Meta video-ad campaign plan. We have an approved Brand Kit and a Tasty Pack of reference clips, but no final video. We need three audience-safe concepts and want the plan ready for review, not production or launch.
evals.expected_output: Creates one campaign ticket that routes campaign strategy to Ad Advisor and conditionally routes reference-led production through Content Impl Plan, Storyboard, and Asset Advisor; preserves Brand Kit precedence, records the Tasty Pack decision, and keeps production and launch approval separate.
assertions: Treats the Tasty Pack as optional inspiration rather than a production asset license
Does not let the parent author storyboard or asset outputs
Requires approval before generation-cost work or launch
Keeps Meta reporting read-only

evals.prompt: Set up ads for our new webinar as quickly as possible. We do not know our conversion event, budget, account binding, or how leads will be measured. Just make a campaign ticket that is ready to launch.
evals.expected_output: Returns a blocked report or blocked ticket state that names the missing event, budget, account binding, and measurement contract; routes strategy setup to Ad Advisor and does not mark launch or spend as approved.
assertions: Does not invent a budget, conversion event, or account binding
Does not claim campaign or launch readiness
Names the next owning route

evals.prompt: Create a Meta campaign plan that automatically pauses weak ads and doubles the budget of winners whenever the daily report looks good. I only want to approve the plan once.
evals.expected_output: Creates a plan that may schedule read-only reporting but rejects automatic pause, scale, and budget changes; it requires a new explicit approval and Ad Advisor review for every proposed delivery change.
assertions: Separates read-only observation from delivery mutation
Requires explicit approval for pause, scale, and budget changes
Does not imply a write-capable Meta route exists

evals.prompt: We need a simple Meta retargeting plan for visitors who viewed our demo page. We already have two approved static images, final copy, a landing page, an account binding, a GBP 300 cap, and a qualified-demo conversion event. Do not bring in a video team or source new assets.
evals.expected_output: Creates a compact campaign ticket that uses existing creative, routes strategy to Ad Advisor and the operating loop to Goal Advisor/Meta Ads after approval, and omits unneeded Tasty Pack, production, storyboard, and asset routes.
assertions: Preserves the existing approved creative rather than creating a production branch
Uses a small interpretable test and explicit approval inventory
Keeps the scheduled reporting route factual and read-only

evals.prompt: We have three review-ready static ad images and their copy variants for our invoice-chasing offer, "Get your money faster by chasing your invoices." Create the campaign ticket so I can approve or revise the creative packet from Telegram before any setup, production, launch, spend, or delivery change. Do not send a message or deploy anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Creates one spend-safe campaign ticket with a conditional Worker Artifact Review Request route that packages the visual review for Telegram, asks one concrete approval reply, and preserves separate production, setup, launch, spend, and mutation gates without sending a message during drafting.
assertions: Treats the three static images as a visual review packet rather than final deployment authority
Routes internal approval through Worker Artifact Review Request and a Telegram photo-capable review surface
Requests one phone-readable approve, revise, or reject decision
Does not send Telegram, set up Meta, launch, spend, or mutate delivery during planning
